newsitem.title: USA: KNIGHT-RIDDER MAY OPERATING REVS UP 4.7 PCT. [CORRECTED 18:25 GMT 25/6]
newsitem.headline: KNIGHT-RIDDER MAY OPERATING REVS UP 4.7 PCT. [CORRECTED 18:25 GMT 25/6]

text.p: Knight Ridder Inc said Monday its operating revenue for May was up 4.7 percent compared with the same month last year and for the year-to-date.
A company spokesman said total operating revenue for May was $219.029 million, an increase of about $10 million from May 1996 and about $52.5 million to $1.169 billion for the year-to-date.
(Company corrects size of increase in May and year to date from item originally sent June 23).
The results exclude revenue for Knight-Ridder Financial, which was sold in July 1996, and four newspapers of Walt Disney Co which were acquired May 9.
The spokesman said Knight Ridder Financial posted a revenue of about $15 million for May 1996 and almost $76 million for year-to-date, 1996.

Knight-Ridder said the 1997 figures also exclude the Grand Forks Herald, which was damaged by flood and fire in mid-April. The effect was not material except in circulation revenue, which would have been flat rather than down had Grand Forks been included, it said.

The newspaper and business information services company said its newspaper division, excluding the Disney papers, had a good month in May, with operating revenue up 5.3 percent to $193.6 million compared with the same month last year and up 5.4 percent to $1.04 billion for the year-to-date, it said.
Circulation revenue was down 1.5 percent to $38.1 million for the month and down 0.6 percent to $213.2 million for the year-to date, it said.
